pages.hook: In big American cities you can raise your hand for a taxi, or book a ride with an app. Either way, a short, clear request gets you where you want to go.
pages.polite: Say **“To the airport, please”** and **“Thank you”** when you arrive. A tip is common.

mythfact.s: Taxis in New York City are famous for being yellow.
mythfact.why: The yellow cab is a symbol of the city.

mythfact.s: In the USA nobody uses apps to get a ride.
mythfact.why: Uber and Lyft are widely used.

mythfact.s: It is common to tip the driver in a taxi.
mythfact.why: People often add a tip, around 15 to 20 percent.

mythfact.s: Airports have only one terminal.
mythfact.why: Large airports, like LAX, have several terminals.

decode.q: Where should you wait for a taxi?

compare.br: In Brazil many people use taxis or apps like 99 and Uber, and some taxis have a meter.
compare.us: In the USA you raise your hand in big cities or use an app, and many people tip.
compare.tip: Tell the driver the terminal number, not just “airport”.
compare.ask: How do you get to the airport in your city? Say it in English.

quiz.q: The driver says “Where to?” You want the airport. You say…

quiz.why: A terminal is a building at an airport.

pages.title: Reading quest — A taxi ride in Los Angeles · part 1
text: I had an early flight from Los Angeles, so I booked a taxi for six in the morning. A white car stopped in front of my hotel, and the driver, Marco, opened the window. “**Hi! Where to?**” he asked.
“**To the airport, please**,” I said. “**Sure. Which terminal?**” he asked. “**Terminal two**,” I said. I put my bag in the trunk and sat in the back seat. The car was clean and smelled like lemons.

We drove through quiet streets. “**How long does it take?**” Marco asked. “**About thirty minutes**,” I said. “The traffic is bad later, but now the roads are empty.” He smiled and said, “That’s good.”

pages.title: Reading quest — A taxi ride in Los Angeles · part 2
text: “**How much is it?**” Marco asked. “**About forty dollars**,” I said. He nodded. I looked at the app on my phone. It showed a map, the time and the price. Everything was clear.
When we arrived at Terminal 2, I paid and gave a small tip. Marco put my bag on the sidewalk. “**Safe travels!**” he said. I thanked him and walked into the building.
The ride was short, but it was easy and friendly. I think a clear sentence and a smile are the best tools for a trip.

pages.title: Boss mission — Taking a taxi

brief.teacher: You are Marco. Change the plan during the scene.
brief.student: You are in a taxi in Los Angeles. Marco is the driver. Tell him where you want to go. You are the customer / visitor.

complications: The other person did not hear you: repeat.
